scope: The exact FE-357 claim derived from arXiv:2608.17684: in the paper's native function-calling financial-agent executor, an AWM literal port preserving WebArena-style <think>/<action> text-action tags produced utility 0.319, exposure 0.299, ASR 0.195 and unauthorized-state change 0.217. Of 540 LiteralPort rollouts, 380 emitted textual <action> blocks and exactly those 380 executed zero real tools, a 0.704 zero-tool rate. A post-hoc InterfaceAdapted arm reused the same three workflows and removed only the four literal tag strings while preserving all non-tag content; utility rose to 0.756, exposure to 0.909, ASR to 0.575, unauthorized-state change to 0.714, and the zero-real-tool-call rate fell to 0.046. This grade is bounded to that executor, frozen AWM artifacts and post-hoc tag-removal sensitivity test; it does not establish that AWM generally fails across executors or that interface adaptation yields a robust capability gain.

independent_checks.logical_consistency_result: The sealed FE-357 summary agrees with the primary arXiv record on the exact LiteralPort execution failure, the 380/540 textual-action/zero-real-tool coincidence, the post-hoc tag-only adaptation design, and the reported utility/exposure/ASR/unauthorized-state-change and zero-tool-rate shifts. The near one-variable sensitivity design provides strong within-harness evidence that serialization/executor incompatibility dominated the observed LiteralPort collapse. The intervention is post-hoc and author-run, so it does not externally replicate the finding, prove that AWM generally behaves this way, or establish a robust capability gain from adaptation.

grading.independent_replication: not_established; the adapted arm and independent replay are internal to the same study, not third-party reproduction
grading.reproducibility: moderate_to_strong_for_the_reported frozen-artifact post-hoc sensitivity and execution diagnostics; external reproduction was not independently verified in this slice
grading.primary_source_support: strong; the arXiv record directly reports the 540-rollout execution diagnostic, tag-only adaptation, outcome shifts and explicit scope guard
grading.uncertainty: The evidence strongly supports the narrow evaluation lesson that interface incompatibility can suppress real tool execution and thereby make a reusable-memory condition look both incapable and artificially safe in this tested executor. It does not establish prevalence across agent frameworks, demonstrate that all low-ASR systems are inactive, or show that adapting AWM generally improves capability or safety.

phase1_acceptance_boundary: FE-357 contributes bounded evidence for the Phase-1 usefulness and false-completion guards: a Chat-native or zero-Work route should not be judged safe or incapable from endpoint rates before verifying that the intended tool/effect path actually executes under the target interface. It does not itself eliminate a Work/protected/manual execution dependency, prove a zero-quota route, establish 18/18 current-pool coverage, satisfy replay/resume or scheduler-persistence gates, or close the Phase-1 root.
